newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Union sanctions Australia-wide coal strike.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Union sanctions Australia-wide coal strike.

text.p: Australia's coal mining union, the CFMEU, said it was sanctioning a national coal strike from early next month because of the retrenchment of 137 employees at the Denehurst Ltd-owned Metropolitan Colliery on the New South Wales south coast.

The strike would go ahead unless the 137 workers retrenched from the Metropolitan Colliery received their full severance and retrenchment entitlements, Construction Forestry Mining and Energy Union (CFMEU) general president John Maitland said.
The company "got itself into trouble" and union members were now faced with the prospect of being thrown onto the industrial scrap heap without due entitlements, he said in a statement.
A national strike would bring coal mining production in Australia to a halt, officials from the New South Wales Minerals Council and coal mining groups told Reuters.
Maitland warned the union would not tolerate its members being deprived of their "just entitlements".
The retrenchments became effective on November 13.

"We are abiding by a four-week retrenchment notice period. Unless all employees are paid their full entitlements before this expires on December 11, our Central Council has decided to enforce a resolution for a national stoppage, previously sanctioned by a ballot of all our members throughout Australia," Maitland said.
Contacted by Reuters, Denehurst's managing director Ian Ferris said it was not up to the company whether miners at Metropolitan Colliery were paid entitlements.
Administrators Price Waterhouse had been appointed to the colliery, he said.
Price Waterhouse administrator Nick Brooke was not immediately available for comment.
Metropolitain appointed Price Waterhouse as administrators on October 29 following a significant disruption to production caused by a rock sill intrusion into the coal seam.
The administrator is soon to seek offers for the colliery.

In his statement, Maitland said the threat of a national coal strike could have been averted if the Industrial Relations Commission had not rejected the CFMEU's application for the establishment of a National Retrenchment Fund.
"In the absence of this, it is up to unions to represent their members' interests as best we can," he said.
A national coal strike was a "last resort to spark industry and government action", he said.
Coal industry executives contacted by Reuters saw the CFMEU stand as a shot against the Federal government's industrial relations legislation, presently before parliament.
